title: Twin Permutations Construction via Complement
approach_explanation:
To satisfy the condition that $a_1 + b_1 
leq a_2 + b_2 
leq 	o 
leq a_n + b_n$, a sufficient and elegant strategy is to make every sum $a_i + b_i$ a constant value. By choosing $b_i = n + 1 - a_i$, we ensure that each sum $a_i + b_i = n + 1$. Because all sums are equal to the same constant, the non-decreasing inequality is trivially satisfied. Furthermore, since $a$ is a permutation of integers from $1$ to $n$, the transformation $b_i = n + 1 - a_i$ maps every distinct element into a distinct element within the same range $[1, n]$, thus guaranteeing that $b$ is also a valid permutation.

code_breakdown.section_title: Test Case Initialization and Input Reading
code_breakdown.explanation: Read the number of test cases $t$, and for each test case, read the size of the permutation $n$ followed by the elements of the array $a$ into a vector $v$.
Define an integer variable `ref` equal to $n + 1$, which represents the target sum for each pair $(a_i, b_i)$.
Iterate through each element of the permutation $a$, compute the corresponding element of $b$ as `ref - v[i]`, and print it immediately to the standard output.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: We iterate through the array of size $n$ twice: once to read the input and once to compute and print the output vector $b$. Thus, the time taken per test case is linear with respect to $n$. Across $t$ test cases, the total time complexity is $O(	extstyle igsum n)$.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: A vector $v$ of size $n$ is allocated for each test case to store the elements of permutation $a$. This requires linear extra space.

strengths: Extremely concise and optimal time/space complexity.
Clever application of constructive logic ensuring all sums are constant.
edge_cases_handled: Works for arbitrary permutations of numbers from $1$ to $n$.

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Instead of storing the entire array $v$ in a vector, we can read elements one by one and print $n + 1 - x$ directly on the fly. This reduces space complexity to $O(1)$ auxiliary space.
